source.title: Risk Bounds for Over-parameterized Maximum Margin Classification on Sub-Gaussian Mixtures
source.authors: Yuan Cao; Quanquan Gu; Mikhail Belkin

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own maximum-margin classifier risk results across feature dimensions. In one tested setting risk worsens as dimension increases, and in another it stays nearly unchanged, contrary to the post-interpolation improvement in V4. It does not test the full double-descent curve.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses double descent in related work but does not test its full shape. Its own Figure 3 varies dimension in over-parameterized settings and explicitly reports dimension-dependent risk trends. Figure 2 varies the mean-vector norm, not a claim axis; the comparisons across n there do not test whether more samples raise risk near an interpolation threshold.
record.test_reason: This is a theory paper on benign overfitting of the maximum-margin linear classifier on sub-Gaussian mixtures. It mentions double descent only in related work and lists verifying it as future work. Its Figure 3 sweep varies data dimension d at fixed n=10 and fixed ||µ||. Raising d there adds noise directions to the data distribution itself, so it does not raise model capacity on a fixed task. Every point is also far past interpolation (d ≥ 100n). Its results therefore do not bear on whether risk improves again past the interpolation threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors prove a population risk upper bound for the maximum-margin classifier on (an)isotropic sub-Gaussian mixtures and show it is tight via matching lower bounds. The bound extends to gradient-descent logistic regression and characterizes when benign overfitting occurs, including dimension-free conditions for α in (1/2,1). Studying dimension versus risk to verify double descent is stated as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives theoretical risk bounds for over-parameterized maximum-margin linear classification and synthetic simulations across selected dimensions; it does not use a full double-descent scaling protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The dimension-risk result differs by covariance-spectrum decay: α = 0.2 shows worse risk at larger d, while α = 0.8 shows nearly unchanged risk. The Figure 3 comparisons use n = 10.

fits_no_version.finding: For max-margin (minimum-norm interpolating) linear classifiers, population risk is small under stated conditions. With α=0.2, larger d gives worse risk; with α=0.8, risk is nearly identical across d = 1000–4000 (n=10).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign overfitting: in over-parameterized linear classification, interpolating max-margin classifiers can attain small risk. Whether added dimensions hurt depends on the covariance spectrum's decay.

record.code_released: Supplementary code is indicated in the checklist, but no URL is stated.
record.problems: The dimension sweep covers only d = 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000 with n = 10, so it does not cover the vicinity of the interpolation threshold or establish a complete curve. Figure 3 values are plotted without exact numerical values or reported uncertainty; the text says the experiments average 100 independent runs.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing results omitted. Figure 2 varies the mean-vector norm and does not measure model size, training time, or sample-size effects near interpolation.

untested.parts: No deep networks; no model-size sweep.
No capacity sweep through the interpolation point on a fixed task; only over-parameterized dimensions on changing distributions.
No effective-complexity predictor of peak location.
No label noise, multiple peaks or regularization tuning studied.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' labels for V4 should be dropped. The paper never traces risk across the interpolation threshold, and its d sweep changes the data distribution rather than model capacity on a fixed task. Coauthor Belkin is an author of an original source (arXiv:1812.11118), but this paper is not itself an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The tested classifier is linear, not a deep network; there is no full model-size sweep through the interpolation threshold.
No training-epoch or training-time risk sweep.
The paper does not sweep sample size near an interpolation threshold to test whether more data raises risk.
The study reports dimension trends only within an over-parameterized range; it does not trace a complete risk curve through the interpolation point.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across axes.
No controlled test of label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
The paper does not recount complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: maximum margin classifier θ̂SVM
rows.operation_detail: Compared population risk across feature dimensions
rows.locator: Appendix D, Figure 3(a), text describing Figure 3
rows.note: The text states that larger d gives worse population risk for α = 0.2. The reported result is aggregated over the dimension sweep; exact risk values are only plotted.
rows.check: Increasing d here changes the data distribution (more noise dimensions, λk = k^-α), not model capacity on a fixed problem. All d values are deep in the over-parameterized regime with no interpolation threshold in range. So the sweep cannot show V4's second descent, and the 'reversed' state is unjustified.

rows.subject: maximum margin classifier θ̂SVM
rows.operation_detail: Compared population risk across feature dimensions
rows.locator: Appendix D, Figure 3(b), text describing Figure 3
rows.note: The text says the risk curves for the different dimensions are almost exactly the same for α = 0.8; exact risk values are only plotted.
rows.check: The same issue as r1 applies. The authors offer the flat curves as evidence of dimension-free risk for α > 1/2 (Corollary 3.5), not as a capacity-versus-risk test. The 'absent' state against V4 is unjustified.
